verdict.rationale: Cloudflare's first-party docs say Workers deploy serverless functions and full-stack apps on Cloudflare's global network with no region complexity, and the Agents SDK docs say Cloudflare runs deployed code across that global network. Community users report Workers are quick and can run in production within an hour. Missing for 10: an explicit first-party statement that code executes at the location nearest each end user, plus PoP coverage or latency figures and independent latency measurements.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run my code on a global edge network close to end users

citations.quote: Build and deploy serverless functions and full-stack apps on Cloudflare's global network. No servers to manage. No cold starts or region complexity.
Deploy once and Cloudflare runs your agents across its global network, scaling to tens of millions of instances.
I've played with JS workers on a Cloudflare-fronted site and found them to be easy to use and very quick.
